summary: Hamilton County lookout at about 1,495 ft; Tennessee Landforms lists it as removed, with its top portion reported at a Bradley County nature center.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed. Its top portion is reported at the Bradley County Ocoee Regional Nature Center; no source describes the original site today.

evidence.supports: top portion now at the Bradley County Ocoee Regional Nature Center
evidence.quote: top portion now resides at Bradley County Ocoee Regional Nature Center

corrections.why: Tennessee Landforms says the top portion now resides at the Bradley County Ocoee Regional Nature Center, so the structure is not wholly gone. A human should decide the wording.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two short entries. No build date, staffing, fires or access were found, so no events are recorded. The nature-center claim rests on one remark on the Tennessee Landforms waypoint, which credits a named reference; check with the nature center before publishing. OpenStreetMap elevation tag is 453 m against 1,495 ft (455.7 m) on Tennessee Landforms; small difference, not changed. CrimeRadar dispatch summaries mention a 'Fire Tower Road' near Ooltewah; they are AI-generated, so not used. Searches used: 2. Pages read: the waypoint, the OpenStreetMap node and one Wikipedia page for Ooltewah with no tower history.
